To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the charge states of Ne, Ar, Kr and Xe in lunar ilmenite samples are in the range from 1.2 to 3.2, 2.0 to 5.0, 3.2 to 7.0 and 5.6 to 8.0, respectively.
the charge states of Ne, Ar, Kr and Xe in lunar ilmenite grains are determined by the cosmic-ray exposure age of the grains and the intensity of the solar proton flux.
the average charge state of inert gas ions is lower in lunar ilmenite grains with higher cosmicray exposure age.

there is no evidence that solar flares have changed significantly over the past billion years.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the solar proton spectrum was harder ∼1 billion year ago than it is today.
the solar activity was higher 2-3 billion years ago and was lower 1 billion years ago, as inferred from the data of lunar samples of different exposure age and the charge states of ions.
the solar proton spectrum in the 1-10 MeV energy range was harder in the past, and the solar flare activity was higher, than now.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the charge states of ions in the ilmenite are determined by a combination of the ionization energy of the inert gas ion and its mass.

the charge states of noble gas ions in lunar minerals are not only determined by the energy spectrum of the primary solar cosmic-ray particles but also by the chemical composition of minerals, and thus, the charge states of the ions in lunar minerals may provide additional information on the history of solar cosmic-ray activity.
